visible_evidence: Faint show-through and stamp. Large separate notation “[1602] April 10.” No letter opening or cipher assigned here.

Stamped 151, with another number 383. Letter begins “I have receaued too letters … one of the 2 of May … / other of the 28”. Inline after Mr near the right end of line 2 is a short group resembling “2nerix”. No passage of sustained symbolic cipher or chain of interlinear glosses.

Continuation in the same hand and syntax at “is out, but promiseth …”. Near close is a string beginning 2 and continued with letter-like shapes, approximately “2 geymshno”; exact individual letterforms uncertain. Immediately follows with “this first of June / wᵗʰ vs.” A name written out reads Harry Wicham; further plaintext notes below and beside it.
Stamped 152, with another number 385. Largely blank. Folds, faint marks, stamp offset and numbers at the foot.

Address and later endorsement on folded exterior. “A Monsʳ / Mounsieur Fransis Direck / marchant en Anvers.” Orthography retained approximately; the consonant after the initial D visually resembles i, not a modern normalized spelling. Larger, separate writing above: “1602 April 10 / Enclosures”.

Stamped 153, separate short letter on a visibly shorter leaf. Begins “I perceaue I have put yᵘ to silence” and closes “adieu 21 of September”, signed “Ha: Wicham”. Mid-body mixture of plaintext, numeral groups, two extended graphic runs, and short interlinear writing. Marginal annotations separate.
